title: Introduce smart prefetch + credential safeguard profiles and align streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Teams have been running into two recurring pain points: (1) tail latency spikes during long-lived streaming sessions caused by cold KV/cache misses and kernel scheduling at the first few token windows; (2) subtle token/credential expiry races when SDKs concurrently refresh credentials during sustained streaming. This PR introduces a coordinated, cross-SDK solution: a smart prefetch algorithm to warm KV/cache and a credential-safeguard profile to serialize refresh windows with graceful handoff. It also harmonizes the consumer API ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go to reduce onboarding friction for multi-language teams.

What this PR delivers (summary): 1) smart-prefetch: an adaptive warmup that prefetches model KV segments and primes the tokenization path for the expected initial sequence length distribution (low overhead; only triggers on streams with >1s expected duration). It uses a lightweight heuristic-based predictor plus an optional telemetry hint from the user (`prefetch_hint`) to trade a small upfront compute cost for stable tail latencies. 2) credential-safeguard profiles: introduces three named profiles (steady/agile/conservative) that define TTL windows, staggered refresh offsets, and handoff semantics to avoid thundering refreshes and token races during reconnects. 3) retry-presets: adds deterministic jittered backoff presets tuned for streaming connections (stream-aware retry that preserves idempotency guarantees for pull/push styles). 4) ergonomics: aligns stream consumer surface (ChunkStream in TS/Go, chunk_stream in Python) with unified async iterator semantics and explicit `prefetch` and `checkpoint` hooks to make interruption and resume flows predictable. 5) cross-SDK version bumps: Python -> 1.12.0, TypeScript -> 2.8.0, Go -> v0.15.0.

Motivation and design notes: The solution balances three goals: minimize user-visible regressions, keep CPU/GPU cost impact minimal, and avoid adding global locks that could block high-throughput clients. Smart-prefetch only activates when heuristics indicate benefit; telemetry gating allows customers to opt-in until wider rollout. Credential-safeguard uses a lease-based handoff (non-blocking) where an outgoing token keeps a short grace window to serve inflight requests while a new token takes over for new streams; this avoids 401 storms at refresh boundaries. Retry-presets are conservative by default; users can opt-in to more aggressive profiles for low-latency experimental workloads.

Files changed (high level): - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py: add chunk_stream, prefetch_hint param, credential profile hooks - sdk/python/redwood/credentials.py: credential-safeguard profiles + TTL engine - sdk/ts/src/stream/chunkStream.ts: ChunkStream API + prefetch hook - sdk/ts/src/credentials/safeguard.ts: JS profile implementation - sdk/go/stream/chunk_stream.go: Go iterator + prefetch support - sdk/go/auth/safeguard.go: go credential profile + lease handoff - internal/telemetry/prefetch_metrics: new metrics & events - tests/*: integration tests for prefetch + refresh scenarios - docs/sdk/migrations: migration notes and examples

Commits: ["a1f8b2f: introduce smart-prefetch predictor and tests", "b3d9c0e: add credential-safeguard profile engine (py)", "c4e7d5a: TS ChunkStream + prefetch hook and docs", "d2f1e97: Go ChunkStream iterator and credential lease handoff", "e5a8b33: add retry-presets (stream-aware), update CI matrix", "f7b4a1c: update release notes and bump versions"]

Testing & CI: All unit and integration tests were added and run. CI matrix includes py3.9/3.11, node16/18, go1.20/1.21. One flaky test in the first run (integration/stream_resume_test) failed due to environment DNS flakiness; rerun succeeded. Performance microbenchmarks show median tail P99 latency reduction of 20-28% for warmup-sensitive workloads and <3% added token cost on short sessions when prefetch is inactive.

Backward compatibility & migration: APIs are additive. Existing streaming consumers continue to work unchanged. Migration notes in docs/sdk/migrations explain renames: Python `StreamCursor` -> `chunk_stream` (compat shim provided for one release), TS/Go new `ChunkStream` constructor accepts old config shape. Credential-safeguard profiles default to `steady` which mirrors prior behavior.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc vetted with Runtime and SRE - [x] Linear tasks completed ENG-2049, ENG-2068 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs & migrations added - [x] SDK version bump and changelogs updated

Risks & follow-ups: - Telemetry gating will be monitored for unexpected CPU/GPU utilization; we may tune heuristics after rollout. - We will run a controlled canary for Dedicated customers before org-wide rollout. - Add a customer-facing control in Console to toggle prefetch per API key if needed.

References: Linear ENG-2049 (stream prefetch), ENG-2068 (credential handoff), support ticket SUP-4012 (customer incident showing concurrent refresh storms).

release_notes: Added smart prefetch for streams to reduce tail latency; introduced credential-safeguard profiles to avoid refresh storms; aligned streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go; bumped SDK versions (py 1.12.0, ts 2.8.0, go v0.15.0).
notes_for_release: Ship notes include migration steps for chunk stream renames, how to opt into prefetch, and guidance for choosing credential profiles. Recommend canary on Dedicated and monitoring prefetched_keys and auth_refresh events.
